era.title: Queen's Tower Opens, May 1893
era.summary: Queen Victoria formally opened the Imperial Institute on 10 May 1893, and its central tower rose 287 feet above a frontage of roughly 700 feet. The exterior used Portland Whitbed stone with contrasting brickwork, and Imperial Institute Road had been laid out south of the building in 1888–92. Work was still finishing: the Survey records labour disputes in 1890–91 and building near completion early in 1894. The record is thin in places — no verified 1893 admission prices, local fares or attendant uniform, and the surviving photographs have no securely established 1893 exposure date.
funFacts: The central tower rose to 287 feet, and its base walls were nine feet thick.
The official opening used a temporary hall; the proposed great hall was never built.
The tower's ten bells were cast by John Taylor of Loughborough.
A billiard-room was added in 1893 to attract subscribing Fellows.
The tower formed the centre of a roughly 700-foot frontage with smaller towers at both ends.
Domed entrances to the Eastern and Western Galleries were built in 1891.

sceneBrief.description: Exactly the framing of the photograph: standing on Imperial Institute Road looking west and slightly up, a long building front running diagonally from the left edge into the distance, the tower rising behind it on the right with its dome against the sky. In 1893 the long building on the left is the brand-new Imperial Institute's ornate south frontage, in the same position and perspective as the modern library: pale Portland stone banded with red brick, rows of tall round-arched windows, carved friezes, gables and small domed turrets along the roofline. The central tower on the right is the same tower, new and clean, its copper dome bright copper-brown, not yet green. A clear sky with light smoke haze.

persists: The central tower's upper masonry and domed silhouette, allowing for later repair.
altered: The tower's base, here integrated into the Institute frontage rather than the later rebuilt freestanding base.
notYetBuilt: Modern campus blocks and landscaped space occupying the demolished Institute footprint.
trees in front of the frontage

sceneBrief.surroundings: To the north the tower and connected frontage dominate, blocking any view through to the rear galleries and gardens. East and west the frontage and carriage road continue laterally — do not replace the wings with open lawn. To the south, the road and its opposite frontage must be reconstructed from a period plan that is still missing from this dossier; the Royal College of Science building is not yet there, but that is not evidence the southern plot was bare. Do not invent southern buildings, shop signs or planting. The rearward view therefore has lower confidence than the documented forward view.

guide.name: Thomas Meecham
guide.role: Mason on the Institute's finishing works
guide.bio: I've been setting and dressing stone on this building while the last of the work is brought to a finish. My days are dust and mortar and the ring of chisels, but I never tire of looking up at that tower.
guide.appearance: Man of about forty, lean and broad-shouldered from years of lifting stone, weathered face and short dark beard. Wears a dark jacket, a rounded brimmed hat, a work-worn waistcoat and sturdy trousers with dusty boots; his hands are rough and pale with stone dust.
guide.script: Thomas Meecham, that's me, mason on the Institute's finishing works. The Queen herself opened the place on the tenth of May, and fine it looked for the day, though plenty of us were still at it after. That central tower stands two hundred and eighty-seven feet, and the walls at its base are nine feet thick, so there's substance to it. They rang the ten bells cast by John Taylor of Loughborough, and the sound carried. There's a billiard-room opened this year too, meant to draw in subscribing Fellows. Mind the delivery carts in the road. Good day to you, and take care on the kerb.
guide.greeting: Morning to you. I'm Thomas Meecham, mason on the Institute's finishing works — mind the carts as you cross, and have a look up at that tower.
